sources.title: P. G. Bissiri, C. C. Holmes, and S. G. Walker, A general framework for updating belief distributions, JRSS B 78(5), 2016
sources.locator: Complete 32-page arXiv full-text preprint, inspected §§1.1–1.2, §2.3, and §§3.1–3.4, including equations (3), (7), and (8); compared with the final publisher PDF.
sources.reading_verification: Read the full text and the complete relevant derivations: §1.1's Bayesian update formulation; §1.2's loss-based update and consistency/sequential coherence; §2.3's additive loss and coherence equation; and §§3.1–3.4's loss scale, unit-information, hierarchical and elicitation proposals. An institutional mirror request returned HTTP 403; the same work's complete arXiv PDF was retrieved and inspected, and the final publisher PDF was also accessible in the web reader. The paper motivates the local claims; every local normalization and KL argument is proved in the carriers.

contents.name: §1.1–§1.2 and equation (7): normalized loss update from prior belief and loss
contents.reason: The definition states the fixed-observation measurable-loss formula and finite-positive normalizer explicitly, while making no sampling-model or likelihood claim.

contents.name: Equation (8): loss-plus-KL minimization characterization
contents.reason: The theorem proves the Gibbs KL decomposition and equality case for its stated absolute-continuity and finite-objective class, rather than importing unverified integrability conditions.

contents.name: Equation (3) and §2.3: sequential coherence for additive losses
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the finite-sequence identity by induction under a fixed positive temperature and finite-positive sequential normalizers.

contents.name: §§3.1–3.4: scale and unit-information, hierarchical, subjective, and interval-matching temperature proposals
contents.reason: The remark records each proposal with its additional reference-law or elicitation input and states that the update theorem alone yields neither robustness nor frequentist coverage.

contents.name: §1.1–§1.2 and equation (7): likelihood-based loss recovers the Bayesian update
contents.reason: The example verifies the likelihood-loss identity from its finite joint table and does not rely on the source for a missing conditional-probability calculation.

contents.name: §§1.2 and 3.1: loss scale and temperature jointly determine the update
contents.reason: The example computes both two-point updates and proves equality after joint rescaling and strict inequality at distinct effective temperatures.

contents.name: §1.1–§1.2: normalization requires a finite positive loss normalizer
contents.reason: The example constructs a proper dyadic prior and proves directly from simple-function lower bounds that its loss normalizer is infinite.

contents.name: §§3.1–3.4: temperature selection proposals and their additional design assumptions
contents.reason: The finite counterexample establishes zero coverage directly; the source's calibration discussion is not used as a coverage theorem.
